metadata.section: INCORPORATING BOTH INDIVIDUAL AND GROUP INFORMATION
subsections: INCORPORATING BOTH INDIVIDUAL AND GROUP INFORMATION
metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: Given that group selection always results in an expected positive response, while individual selection can range from (at best) being far more efficient than group selection to (at worst) generating an expected reversed response, clearly the optimal approach is some combination of selection on both individual and group components. This is simply an extension of the concept of a family index introduced in Chapter 21, that combines both individual and family (now group) information.
